Introduction to Putnam County, Missouri

Putnam County sits in north central Missouri near the Iowa border. The county seat is Unionville. It is a quiet rural county with farmland, timber land, and small towns. Property taxes help support schools, roads, and local services.

When taxes go unpaid, the county sells a tax lien certificate at a public auction. This process allows the county to collect overdue taxes. It also gives investors a chance to earn interest or gain property rights if taxes remain unpaid.

This guide explains how the Putnam County tax sale works. It covers the auction schedule, bidding process, redemption period, and investor steps. The goal is to help investors understand how to participate in the Putnam County, Missouri tax lien auction.

What Is Putnam County’s Tax Lien Investing System?

Missouri counties use a tax lien certificate sale system. When property taxes remain unpaid, the county sells the tax debt to an investor. The winning bidder pays the delinquent taxes and receives a certificate.

The property owner then has time to repay the taxes plus interest and fees. This period is called the redemption period. If the owner redeems, the investor receives their money back with interest. If the owner does not redeem after multiple sale stages, the investor may move toward obtaining a tax deed.

Putnam County follows Missouri state law for these auctions. The county collector runs the sale each year.

Important Details

Key Takeaways
  • Putnam County, Missouri, offers a tax lien certificate sale system to collect overdue property taxes.
  • Investors can participate in annual auctions, typically held on the fourth Monday in August, to bid on delinquent properties.
  • The redemption period allows property owners to pay their taxes plus interest, while investors can earn up to 10% in returns in the first year.
  • Conducting due diligence, such as checking property details and potential liens, is crucial to avoid risky investments.
  • Putnam County appeals to both local and foreign investors due to its stable property tax system and lower competition in rural areas.

Fun Facts About Putnam County

Putnam County has a small population and a strong farming history. The county is known for its open land and quiet lifestyle.

• Population is about 4,500 residents.
• Unionville has served as the county seat since the 1800s.
• Agriculture remains the main economic activity.
• Land prices are lower than many areas in Missouri.

This history means many properties are rural parcels or small homes. That can create interesting tax lien opportunities.

Auction Process for Tax Lien Sales

Putnam County runs a public tax lien certificate auction each year. The county collector manages the sale.

Investors compete for tax liens tied to delinquent property taxes. The winning bidder pays the taxes owed. They receive a tax certificate.

Missouri uses a bid down interest system. The maximum interest rate starts at 10 percent for the first year. Investors bid by lowering the interest rate they are willing to accept.

How the Auction Works

• Review the delinquent property list before the auction
• Attend the tax sale at the county courthouse
• Listen as the collector calls each property
• Investors bid the lowest interest rate they will accept
• The lowest interest bid wins the certificate
• The winning bidder pays the full tax amount due

Missouri law also allows second and third tax sales in later years if properties remain unsold.

Maximum Potential Returns and Expected Returns on Putnam County Tax Lien Certificates

The maximum interest rate for a Missouri tax lien certificate is 10 percent during the first year. The property owner must pay the delinquent taxes plus the interest rate set at the auction.

Returns depend on several factors.

If bidding competition is low, an investor may secure a higher interest rate. If competition is strong, investors may bid the interest rate down.

Additional penalties and fees may apply during redemption. These payments increase the total amount returned to the investor.

In some cases, the property owner does not redeem the lien. When this happens, the investor may move toward obtaining ownership after the proper legal steps.

Open to All Investors and Foreign Participation

Missouri tax lien sales are open to the public. Both local and international investors may participate.

Many counties hold the auction in person. Investors must attend the sale or send a representative.

Foreign investors can still participate by following the same rules as local bidders. They must pay the winning bid amount and follow Missouri tax sale laws.

The state has seen increasing interest from investors across the country. Some investors also travel from outside the United States to attend tax lien auctions.

This open system creates global investment opportunities for buyers who want exposure to U.S. real estate backed tax liens.

Importance of Due Diligence in Putnam County Tax Lien Investing

What Due Diligence Entails

• Check the property location and parcel information
• Review assessor data for property size and use
• Confirm if other liens exist on the property
• Inspect the area if possible
• Review zoning and land use restrictions

These steps help investors avoid buying unwanted properties.

Risks of Skipping Due Diligence

• The property may be landlocked
• The parcel may be unusable or flooded
• Structures may be damaged or abandoned
• Additional liens may affect the title

Research helps reduce investment risks.

Buying Over the Counter Tax Liens in Putnam County

Some properties remain unsold during the tax auction. These may later become available directly from the county.

How to Purchase OTC Liens

Contact the county collector’s office. Ask for the current delinquent property list. If a property has passed through previous sale stages, it may be available outside the auction.

Investors usually pay the outstanding tax amount plus interest and fees.

Benefits of OTC Purchases

OTC purchases allow investors to buy liens without bidding competition. Interest rates may remain fixed. Investors also have time to review properties before buying.

Conclusion

Putnam County runs an annual tax lien certificate auction to collect unpaid property taxes. Investors can attend the courthouse sale and bid on delinquent properties.

The auction usually takes place on the fourth Monday in August. Investors bid down the interest rate to win the tax lien certificate. The property owner then has time to redeem the lien by paying the taxes and interest.

Missouri tax lien certificates can produce solid returns when the owner redeems. If the owner fails to redeem after the legal process, investors may move toward ownership rights.

Even with these opportunities, research is still important. Investors should review property details, location, and possible title issues before bidding.

With careful planning and proper due diligence, Putnam County tax lien investing can offer consistent opportunities for both new and experienced investors.

Pro Tips

• Visit the county before the sale if possible. Rural parcels can vary greatly in quality.
• Focus on properties near towns or roads for better resale value.
• Study the assessor database before the auction day.
• Track properties that appear in multiple tax sales. These sometimes present strong deals.
• Bring certified funds so payment can be completed quickly after winning bids.

FAQs About Putnam County Tax Lien Investing

Can I renovate a property after receiving a tax lien certificate?

No. Renovation usually requires ownership through a tax deed process.

Do tax liens remove mortgages automatically?

No. Title research is needed before claiming ownership.

Can I sell my tax lien certificate?

Yes. Investors sometimes assign or sell certificates privately.

What if someone lives on the property?

Occupancy issues must be handled after ownership rights are obtained.

Can I finance tax lien purchases?

Most counties require full payment at the auction.
